cells.tense: You're here, and the setup is yours.
cells.verb: tending what grows so it keeps growing
cells.place: in the place where you decide how things are arranged
cells.ask: Let one thing you've tended be seen as finished — by someone else — and set it down while they're looking. What comes back is care that doesn't wear you out: holding the shape without gripping it.
cells.core: You're here, and the setup is yours. The way things are arranged around you isn't a cage and it isn't an accident — you built it so what matters could keep growing, and you adjust it when the growing changes. Two things pull on you at once and you keep both alive without picking a favorite. That's rarer than it looks from inside. The next thing this is free to do is be seen: let one thing you've tended be called finished, by someone else, and set it down while they're looking. What comes back is care that doesn't wear you out — holding the shape without gripping it.
cells.sheetLine: You built the frame so things could grow, and you keep adjusting it.

cells.tense: You're already living in the version where it all falls apart if you stop watching.
cells.verb: tending what grows until the tending is all it does
cells.place: in the place where you decide how things are arranged
cells.ask: Sit for a minute with one thing that already came out the way you pictured it, and let that be the whole task. What comes back is growth that happens without being forced — care that doesn't exhaust, hands open around what's growing.
cells.core: You're already living in the version where it all falls apart if you stop watching. So every arrangement gets a second arrangement, every rule gets a backup, and the things you set up to help something grow have started growing faster than the thing itself. Nothing is actually loose yet — you're bracing for a day that hasn't come. Here's a different motion: sit for a minute with one thing that already came out the way you pictured it, and let that be the whole task. Not the next fix. What comes back is growth that happens without being forced — care that doesn't exhaust, hands open around what's growing.
cells.sheetLine: You're tightening the frame on a collapse that hasn't happened.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: letting what grows run wild because the tending stopped
cells.place: in the place where you decide how things are arranged
cells.ask: Pick one thing you still want, say the wanting out loud, and keep saying it this week — let the arrangement grow around that, instead of trying to rebuild the arrangement first. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust: a shape you hold without clutching.
cells.core: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you. Somewhere back there the way things were set up stopped working, and instead of changing it you stepped back from the whole job — now things are running on an old arrangement nobody's tending, and you can see it drifting. The empty place isn't where to push. Pick one thing you still want, say the wanting out loud, and keep saying it this week — let the arrangement grow around that, instead of trying to rebuild the arrangement first. What comes back is care that doesn't exhaust: a shape you hold without clutching.
cells.sheetLine: You stepped back from tending it, and it's drifting on an old plan.

cells.tense: You've got the pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: tending what grows and calling it the way things are
cells.place: in the place where you decide how things are arranged
cells.ask: Say what one arrangement you keep was for — out loud, to the person it was for. What comes back is holding space without clutching it: the care gets to be yours, and it gets lighter for being seen.
cells.core: You've got the pen down in a room you're already writing. The way things are arranged around you — what gets done first, what gets protected, what quietly isn't allowed — people lean on that every day, and it's yours. You talk about it like weather, like it just is how things go. The tending is happening; the one doing it hasn't signed. Try the simpler, earlier form: say what one arrangement you keep was for, out loud, to the person it was for. What comes back is holding space without clutching it — the care gets to be yours, and it gets lighter for being seen.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one holding the frame. You call it just how it is.
